 Lyon R2 previews and predictions: Cobolli vs. Wawrinka, Fritz vs. Herbert 
 October 21, 2026 
 Ricky 
 Match previews 
 7 
 Andrew Patron/Delray Beach Open 
 Stan Wawrinka battled to a big win in Lyon on Wednesday and his reward is a second-round showdown against top seed Flavio Cobolli on Thursday. Taylor Fritz and Pierre-Hugues Herbert are also aiming for a place in the quarterfinals.
 (1) Flavio Cobolli vs. (WC) Stan Wawrinka
Cobolli and Wawrinka will be squaring off for the third time in their careers when they collide in round two of the Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes on Thursday. Both of their previous encounters have gone Cobolli’s way, but it hasn’t been easy. The Italian prevailed 6-7(6), 7-6(4), 6-3 at the 2024 Shanghai Masters and 6-4, 6-7(2), 7-6(4) at the 2026 United Cup.
Speaking of thrillers, Wawrinka outlasted Martin Landaluce 6-3, 6-7(2), 7-6(5) on Wednesday afternoon in Lyon. This is the penultimate event of the 41-year-old Swiss’ illustrious career, and he is still playing well regardless of what his No. 140 ranking indicates. As for Cobolli, the world No. 6 heads into this tournament on a four-match losing streak dating back to round three of the U.S. Open. There is no denying that a two-hour and 46-minute struggle is not ideal for Wawrinka, but at least he has a match under his belt and Cobolli is extremely vulnerable right now. An upset would hardly come as a surprise.
 Pick: Wawrinka in 3

 (Q) Pierre-Hugues Herbert vs. (2) Taylor Fritz
It has already been a very good week for Herbert in front of the home crowd. The 35-year-old Frenchman dismissed Jurij Rodionov and Maxim Mrva in qualifying before beating Sebastian Baez 6-3, 6-4 in round one. That marked Herbert’s first ATP-level victory of the season — his first since Stuttgart in June of 2025, in fact.
Up next for the world No. 290 on Thursday is a second showdown against Fritz, who lost their only previous meeting 7-6(4), 6-4 at the 2018 Miami Masters. Of course, that result is hardly relevant; Fritz was barely more than teenager when they last went head-to-head. The 28-year-old American is now the No. 14 player in the world and in outside contention for another trip to the Nitto ATP Finals. Fritz will need a big result in either Basel or Paris (or both), but every point helps at this stage — so the second seed should be very motivated to lift the Lyon trophy. For now, Fritz will be focused on a second-round match that he should win with ease.
 Pick: Fritz in 2
